findings.evidence: fetch_url maps rec.fetch_status == REFUSED to the fixed message 'URI will not fetch that address (private or local network).' SafeFetcher also uses REFUSED for DNS_FAILED, DNS_EMPTY, PORT_REFUSED, URL_INVALID and HOST_INVALID. Probe with a resolver raising socket.gaierror for 'http://typo-domain-xyz.com/' returned {'status':'unavailable','message':'URI will not fetch that address (private or local network).','refusal_code':'DNS_FAILED'}. The production tool gives the same for a host of 5x63-char labels (DNS_FAILED), and 'https://example.com:8443/x' gives PORT_REFUSED with the same message. The baseline reported an unresolvable host as 'URI could not reach that URL.' The module docstring promises to report the real reason; a typo'd or offline domain is now told to the user as a private-network address.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the private/local message only for address-class codes (ADDRESS_NOT_PUBLIC, ADDRESS_TRANSITION_REFUSED, HOST_LOCAL_NAME, HOST_NUMERIC_AMBIGUOUS, USERINFO_REFUSED). Map DNS_FAILED and DNS_EMPTY to 'URI could not reach that URL.', and PORT_REFUSED, SCHEME_REFUSED and URL_INVALID to accurate wording. Keep refusal_code and do not add the address. Add tests for DNS failure and port refusal messages.
findings.title: Every REFUSED status, including DNS failure, port refusal and invalid URL, is reported as a 'private or local network' address

findings.evidence: Mock 200 text/html with content-encoding: gzip returns {'status':'unsupported','message':"URI has no reader for content type 'unknown'.",'content_type':''}. The baseline (requests) decompressed it transparently and returned the text. Accept-Encoding: identity makes this rare.
findings.suggested_fix: Report the real reason (unsupported content encoding) or keep the content type, so an HTML page is not called 'unknown'.
findings.title: Content-Encoding gzip response is reported as unsupported content type 'unknown'

findings.evidence:
Mock text/html (no charset, no meta) with Latin-1 body b'

caf\xe9

' gives text 'caf\ufffd'. The baseline used requests' response.encoding (ISO-8859-1 for text/*) and gave 'café'. The reverse case (UTF-8 bytes without a charset) improves. This is a small output change under S-AC5 'public HTML unchanged'.
findings.suggested_fix: Accept and record the change in the plan, or fall back to latin-1 when UTF-8 decoding fails.
findings.title: HTML without a charset is now decoded as UTF-8 instead of ISO-8859-1

findings.evidence: kind = extra or TEXT_TYPES.get(mime). With fetch_url's map, text/plain becomes 'document', so _robots_allows (res.kind == 'text') would never parse robots.txt if robots were enabled on that fetcher. Not reachable today because fetch_url passes robots=False.
findings.suggested_fix: Document that extra_types must not be used with robots, or keep robots.txt fetches on TEXT_TYPES only.
findings.title: extra_types overrides TEXT_TYPES, which silently changes robots.txt handling for such a fetcher
